brief.analysis: Measured against its own upward trend rather than a flat line, defense-versus-stocks is barely stretched at all — the plain and trend-adjusted readings disagree by more than the usual margin, which is direct evidence the average itself is marching higher, not a temporary spike. That fits the world: global military spending hit a record ~$2.9 trillion in 2025, rising for an 11th straight year with Europe up double digits. With no trend confirmation (0 of 3), a coin-flip hit rate, and the near-term target already reached, the reversion target to the 5-year norm is chasing a mean that has moved.
brief.report_line: We are passing on the short of defense stocks versus the market: the trend-adjusted reading shows the relationship's baseline is drifting upward on a durable global rearmament cycle, not snapping back.

brief.analysis: The case that chips have permanently re-rated versus the broad Nasdaq is strong: AI data-center spending is a multi-trillion-dollar build-out, with the big four cloud players raising capital budgets over 40% in 2025 and chips taking ~60% of every dollar spent. Chipmakers are still running ahead of the Nasdaq on both a plain and a trend-adjusted basis, their 50-day average is still rising against a short position, and confirmation signals are weak (1 of 3). The target that would send this back to its 5-year average implies a ~70% move — that number describes a different era, not a tradeable dislocation.
brief.report_line: We are declining the short of chipmakers versus the Nasdaq: they remain stretched and still rising, and the reversion target ignores a genuine, still-accelerating AI hardware spending cycle.

brief.analysis: The strongest case against betting gold gives back its lead over stocks is that central banks have become permanent, price-insensitive buyers — they bought roughly 850 tonnes in 2025, well above the historic norm of ~470, and gold has now overtaken US Treasuries as the world's largest reserve asset by value. The easy part of this trade is already done (the near-term one-year-average target has been hit); what remains is the pull back to the 5-year average, and that average was set before this buying wave and is probably too low a target now. Trade the snap-back that already happened, not the last leg down to a mean that has likely moved up.
brief.report_line: We are short gold versus US stocks after gold's spike, but only for the completed near-term move — the pull all the way back to its 5-year norm is unlikely because sustained central-bank buying has structurally raised gold's floor.

brief.analysis: The mechanics here are the cleanest of the book — full trend confirmation (3 of 3), the short-term average has rolled over, and the near-term target is already met — and because this pits silver against gold, gold's own structural strength partly offsets the regime worry. But silver went vertical in 2025 (up roughly 150% at its peak, called 'unhinged' by one bank's strategists), so the near-term give-back is believable while the full ~17% slide to the 5-year norm assumes a calm that mania markets rarely deliver. Take the reversion silver has already begun, but size for the risk that the metals surge isn't finished.
brief.report_line: We are short silver versus gold on a clean, confirmed pullback signal, sized down because silver's parabolic 2025 run means the move may not retrace fully to its multi-year norm.

brief.analysis: Metals and miners are in a documented supercycle — the global metals-and-mining index is up roughly 90% since early 2025, beating chips and big tech, driven by copper and AI-and-energy-transition demand — so the 5-year average sits in pre-boom territory that may never be revisited. That said, the trade's near-term signal is real: full confirmation is close (2 of 3), the short-term average has turned, and the one-year-average target is already hit. The trouble is the thin track record (only two comparable episodes) and a ~21% reversion target that assumes the commodity surge reverses. Trade the completed snap-back, not the round-trip to the old norm.
brief.report_line: We are short miners versus the market on a confirmed near-term pullback that has mostly already played out, sized down because an active metals supercycle makes the deeper reversion target questionable and the historical sample is thin.
